meta.note: Good practices were found by web search in November 2026. One-line takeaways are in our own words and based on the page that was read. Items marked as not read were listed from their title and overview page only.

sources.title: Five years of a Greener NHS (NHS England board paper)
sources.takeaway: The Health and Care Act 2022 made England the first health system with net zero in law: net zero by 2040 for direct emissions and 2045 for the wider footprint. By 2024/25 the NHS footprint was about 68% below 1990 and 14% below 2020.

sources.title: Green Deal 3.0: Samen werken aan duurzame zorg (signing announcement)
sources.authors: Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport (VWS)
sources.takeaway: A voluntary deal between government, care providers, insurers and banks: 55% less direct CO2 by 2030 (versus 2018) and climate-neutral care by 2050, across five themes including medicines and circular working.

sources.title: Kenya Climate Change and Health Strategy 2024-2029
sources.authors: Ministry of Health Kenya, with AFIDEP and LSHTM
sources.takeaway: A national strategy with three aims: reduce climate-driven health risks, make health care resilient to climate shocks, and build governance and leadership for climate and health.

sources.title: Uganda unveils its climate and health National Adaptation Plan (H-NAP 2025-2030)
sources.authors: Makerere University School of Public Health
sources.takeaway: Built on the ten components of the WHO framework, with climate-proofed and solar-powered facilities and links to local development planning. Costed at about $63 million to 2030; coordinated through the Office of the Prime Minister.

sources.title: National Action Plan for Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation in the Health Sector 2025-2030
sources.takeaway: Set by ministerial decree. Covers floods, heat-related illness and vector-borne and respiratory disease, with a focus on health system readiness, monitoring of extreme weather and disease, and joining climate and health data in planning.

sources.title: China National Climate Change Health Adaptation Action Plan (2024-2030)
sources.authors: China CDC (summary); issued jointly by 13 departments in September 2024
sources.takeaway: A multi-ministry plan: by 2025 a coordination mechanism and a first round of climate-health risk assessments; by 2030 a policy and standards system, stronger monitoring and early warning, and more resilient health systems.

sources.title: Vulnerability and Adaptation Assessment of Health to Climate Change in Ethiopia
sources.takeaway: An early national V&A with a separate assessment per region, mapping hazards, exposure and adaptive capacity, used as the evidence base for Ethiopia's health adaptation planning.

sources.title: Ethiopia: National Health Adaptation Plan to Climate Change 2018-2020
sources.takeaway: One of the first national health adaptation plans in Africa, following directly on the national V&A.
sources.note: Not read in full; listed from the WHO publication page.

sources.title: Colombia Climate and Health Vulnerability Assessment (2024)
sources.takeaway: Sub-national analysis for all 32 departments with economic cost estimates, covering vector- and water-borne disease, heat, air quality, zoonoses and health system readiness.

sources.title: Health care's climate footprint
sources.authors: Health Care Without Harm and Arup
sources.takeaway: Health care causes about 4.4% of global net emissions; if it were a country it would be the fifth-largest emitter. The baseline many national GHG assessments start from.

sources.title: Evaluating progress and accountability for achieving COP26 Health Programme international ambitions for sustainable, low-carbon, resilient health-care systems
sources.takeaway: Looks at how far countries have turned their COP26 health commitments into action and how accountability could be improved.

sources.title: The 2026 Europe report of the Lancet Countdown on health and climate change
sources.takeaway: Tracks 43 indicators, seven of them new. Heat-related deaths rose in nearly all regions, while political, media and public engagement with climate and health declined.

sources.title: Science and policy experts unite in Africa to accelerate climate and health solutions
sources.country: South Africa, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Ghana, Senegal
sources.takeaway: £40 million for two regional hubs (led by Wits and KNUST) that bring researchers, policymakers and communities together to get local evidence into policy within five years; a third hub for Eastern Africa is planned.

sources.title: Global Consortium on Climate and Health Education
sources.authors: Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health
sources.takeaway: Free certificate courses and teaching resources for health professionals, with 400+ member schools and organisations in 60+ countries, and work on core competencies and accreditation.

sources.title: Lessons from the HealthADAPT program (2018-2022)
sources.takeaway: Ten health authorities built adaptation capacity over four years. Lessons cover six elements: buy-in, foundational resources, data, staff, networks and health equity; senior management support mattered most.

sources.title: HealthADAPT and HeatADAPT (2026)
sources.takeaway: More than $17 million for 24 projects: six on climate-resilient, low-carbon health systems and 18 on extreme heat, including vulnerability assessments, workforce training, heat alerts and indoor heat protection.

sources.title: India's Heat Action Plan: Ahmedabad
sources.takeaway: South Asia's first city heat action plan: local leadership, research on heat deaths, training of health staff, prepared facilities, multi-channel heat alerts and an interagency response. Widely copied by other Indian cities and states.

sources.title: Report of heat-related activities 2024, National Programme on Climate Change and Human Health
sources.authors: NCDC, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare India
sources.takeaway: Documents national and state heat-health work: early warning, public campaigns, intersectoral coordination, training and regional good practices.
sources.note: Summary page read; full report not read.

sources.title: France's heat health watch warning system
sources.authors: Pascal M, Laaidi K, Ledrans M et al.
sources.takeaway: Built after the 2003 heatwave from mortality and weather data in 14 cities: thresholds on combined minimum and maximum temperatures, run jointly by Météo-France, the public health agency and the ministry, and tied to a national action plan since June 2004.

sources.title: Evaluation of the National Heat Plan: risk of dying from heat strongly reduced since 2010
sources.takeaway: Estimated heat-related deaths fell from about 7,000 (2000-2009) to 4,300 (2010-2019) after the National Heat Plan started, with the biggest drops among older people, women and lower-income neighbourhoods.

sources.title: Performance of heat-health warning systems in Shanghai evaluated by using local heat-related illness data
sources.takeaway: Tests how well Shanghai's heat warnings match actual heat-related illness, a model for checking warning thresholds against local health data.

sources.title: Infodengue: a platform for monitoring the transmission of climate-sensitive diseases
sources.takeaway: Weekly arbovirus alerts for about 5,300 Brazilian municipalities, combining weather, social and case data into indicators of receptivity, transmission and outbreak for health authorities.

sources.title: Integrating malaria surveillance with climate data for outbreak detection and forecasting: the EPIDEMIA system
sources.takeaway: Joins routine malaria surveillance with environmental data to detect and forecast malaria outbreaks.

sources.title: Wolbachia dramatically reduces dengue cases (AWED trial, Yogyakarta)
sources.journal: New England Journal of Medicine (trial publication)
sources.takeaway: A cluster-randomised trial in Yogyakarta: releasing Wolbachia mosquitoes cut dengue cases by 77% and dengue hospitalisations by 86%, across all four serotypes.

sources.title: Control of ciguatera poisoning in the Canary Islands (Observatory case study)
sources.takeaway: How the Canary Islands responded to a climate-sensitive marine toxin that is spreading into European waters.
sources.note: Not read; listed from the Observatory overview page.

sources.title: Barcelona tackles mosquito-borne disease risks (Observatory case study)
sources.takeaway: A city programme against the rising risk of mosquito-borne diseases such as dengue in southern Europe.
sources.note: Not read; listed from the Observatory front page.

sources.title: Changing the urban design of cities for health: the superblock model
sources.takeaway: A health impact assessment of Barcelona's superblocks: less traffic, cleaner air, less noise and heat and more green space could prevent several hundred premature deaths a year if the full plan were built.
sources.note: The repository page could not be opened during this build; the figure is given as an order of magnitude only.

sources.title: Four pillars to Hamburg's Green Roof Strategy: financial incentive, dialogue, regulation and science
sources.takeaway: A city green-roof programme combining subsidies, regulation, dialogue and research to cool buildings and manage rainwater.
sources.note: Not read; listed from the Climate-ADAPT heat solutions page.

sources.title: Nature-based solutions in schools: Solana de los Barros, Extremadura
sources.takeaway: Greening a school with nature-based solutions to protect children against heat.
sources.note: Not read; listed from the Observatory overview page.

sources.title: Action for climate change: examples from the WHO Regions for Health Network
sources.takeaway: Regional case studies (Andalusia, Emilia-Romagna, Flanders and others). Lessons: build health into climate policy, strengthen early warning, invest in resilient low-carbon health systems and tackle inequity.

sources.title: Using the Climate and Health Observatory to refine Belgium's National Environment and Health Action Plan
sources.takeaway: Belgium's federal health service used other countries' country profiles, case studies and indicators from the Observatory to benchmark and shape its national plan.

sources.title: Heat and health: experiences from Austria (IANPHI 2025)
sources.takeaway: Austria revised its national heat-health action plan in 2024 in a modular design based on WHO advice, with toolboxes and best practice examples for vulnerable groups and for health and care settings, and a national competence centre on climate and health.

sources.title: Smart Health Care Facilities in the Caribbean: final report
sources.takeaway: 55 facilities retrofitted to be both disaster-safe and green (2015-2023); 28 reached the new A/70 resilience standard. Retrofitting also saved embodied carbon compared with building new.

sources.title: Zimbabwe: 1,044 health facilities now solar-powered
sources.authors: UNDP Solar for Health, Global Fund
sources.takeaway: 11 MW of solar at 1,044 facilities keeps labs, medicine storage and patient care running during power cuts; surplus power goes to the grid.

sources.title: Guideline for assessing climate-resilient and environmentally sustainable health facilities
sources.takeaway: A national tool for facilities to assess their climate vulnerability and footprint, prioritising high-risk facilities and those reporting medical waste.

sources.title: How Bangladesh is beating the odds on climate disaster deaths
sources.takeaway: Cyclone deaths fell from 300,000-500,000 in 1970 to about 3,500 for Sidr in 2007, thanks to the Cyclone Preparedness Programme's 76,000+ volunteers (half women) and growth from 44 to more than 14,000 shelters.

sources.title: South Africa National Heat Health Action Guidelines
sources.authors: National Department of Health South Africa
sources.takeaway: Affordable steps for individuals and communities, the health sector's lead role in heat planning and coordination, and timely information for vulnerable groups.

sources.title: Temperature-related health impacts: a scoping review and benchmarking exercise to inform a heat action plan
sources.authors: Wright CY, Bulani M, Kapwata T et al.
sources.takeaway: Benchmarks Victoria, Maharashtra and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to design Gauteng's plan: local district thresholds keep activation simple; graded activation with clear department roles reduces confusion in long heatwaves.

sources.title: Strengthening climate resilience of the Lao PDR health system: the first Green Climate Fund project on climate and health
sources.takeaway: The first GCF-funded project dedicated to health, showing that health ministries can access large-scale climate finance.

sources.title: Indonesia partners with UNDP and WHO in a Green Climate Fund initiative for climate-resilient health care
sources.takeaway: Launched by the Ministry of Health in May 2024 as part of a 17-country GCF programme: early warning for climate-sensitive diseases plus emission cuts in health facilities.

sources.title: Building the resilience of Togo's national health system and vulnerable communities to climate-sensitive health outcomes (FP305)
sources.takeaway: A recent GCF-approved health resilience project, with GIZ as the implementing organisation.
sources.note: Only the project page was read; amounts and components are in the funding proposal.

sources.title: Global philanthropies commit $300 million to accelerate solutions on climate and health
sources.takeaway: Wellcome, Gates, Bloomberg, Rockefeller and others pledged an initial $300 million for the Belém Health Action Plan, first for extreme heat, air pollution and climate-sensitive infections, and for joining climate and health data.
